title: Seated Calf Raise
summary: Calf raises with the knees bent: the soleus does most of the work (rated 1), while the gastrocnemius can't help much (rated 0.4).

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine).

muscles.why: The calves point the foot (plantar flexion). With the knee bent, the gastrocnemius is slack, so the soleus does most of the work (1 vs 0.4).

region_notes.text: Seated raises grew the gastrocnemius very little, while standing raises grew it far more; soleus growth was similar.

setup.text: Sit with the pad on your lower thighs, just above the knees.
Balls of the feet on the step, heels free to drop.
Release the safety lever before the first rep.

form_cues.cue: Lower the heels to a full stretch
form_cues.why: The deep stretch at the bottom is part of the range.
A short pause at the bottom stops the Achilles from bouncing the weight up.

form_cues.cue: Hold the top for a second
form_cues.why: Full height at the top finishes the range.
Keeps the ankle from rolling out.

bias_tweaks.change: Bias the bottom half at the end of a set
bias_tweaks.effect: Partials at long calf lengths grew the calves more than partials near the top (in standing raises).
bias_tweaks.caveat: That study measured gastrocnemius with standing raises; seated is modeled from it.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.fix: Pause at the bottom and lift without bouncing.
Use the full range with a pause at the bottom.

mistakes.text: Only doing seated raises and expecting full calves.
mistakes.fix: Add a standing raise for the gastrocnemius.

misconceptions.myth: Seated and standing calf raises work the same.
misconceptions.reality: Standing raises grew the gastrocnemius far more; seated raises mainly train the soleus.

misconceptions.myth: Every set has to go to failure to grow.
misconceptions.reality: Stopping a few reps short gave similar growth to failure in a meta-analysis; growth tends to rise as sets get closer to failure, but the exact curve is uncertain.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Easy to push close to failure.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Knee straight, so the gastrocnemius works fully.
Calf raises on the leg press with the knee straight.
Standing raises with the Smith bar: knee straight, heavy loading.

notes: The standing vs seated finding is one 12-week study in 14 untrained adults.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
